analysis.title: Tesla, Inc. Thoughts on recent Robotaxi/Cybercab updates - AV inflection continues
key_insights: Barclays views Tesla's recent Robotaxi and Cybercab updates as broadly supportive of the Robotaxi narrative. Early signs of Robotaxi inflection were one driver of its late-October upgrade.

Tesla announced Robotaxi operations are available 24/7 in all cities. Barclays reads this as technical progress with a camera-only system, given Musk's October comments on sensing difficulty in the dark.
Robotaxi now operates in 8 US cities. Fort Worth launched Nov 2 and San Antonio Nov 9. Geofences expanded about 90% in Miami (Nov 16), about 60% in Austin (Nov 9) and about 10x in Houston (Oct 26).
Tesla reported about 5.4mn autonomous Robotaxi miles as of mid-November, versus 3.1mn through Oct 18. Detailed data has not been provided since the 3Q earnings release.
Tesla and Waymo each had about 1.3k AVs registered with Texas as of mid-November. Barclays expects market share data points for both to emerge as they ramp.
Tesla said Cybertruck production at Gigafactory Texas would end mid-2027 to make room for Cybercab. Musk later clarified production would run through the end of summer 2027.

Tesla disclosed about 125k annual Cybercab capacity at Gigafactory Texas at 3Q EPS, with installed capacity well above that. Barclays estimates Tesla could produce 300-400k+ Cybercab per year there using the Cybertruck footprint.

Barclays calls Cybercab expansion a show-me story. The current Robotaxi footprint needs well below the roughly 125k per year capacity. About half of Tesla's roughly 1.3k Texas AVs are Cybercab and the rest are Model Y.

Tesla announced a roughly $3.3bn Gigafactory Berlin investment for a factory producing up to 1mn Cybercabs a year, with construction starting 1H27 and SOP in 2029. Barclays questions the European need, since Tesla has no Robotaxi presence in Europe and FSD is not approved in the EU. It suspects early volumes will be well below 1mn.

Customer-owned Cybercab will be sold invite-only at about $30k, with deliveries from December 2026, only in Tesla's five existing Texas Robotaxi cities. It can run unsupervised only inside the Robotaxi geofences and for personal use.
Cybercab operation requires a $299/month subscription. Musk said the fee is too high and should be closer to the roughly $115/month cost of FSD plus connectivity on consumer vehicles.

Barclays sees limited TAM for the current customer-owned Cybercab. It calls it a marketing product aimed at Tesla influencers, since it has no steering wheel or pedals and cannot serve as a primary car.
Barclays would expect demand to rise significantly if owners could add Cybercabs to Tesla's Robotaxi fleet and share in profits. It notes open issues on profit splits, servicing and insurance.

Management said at 3Q that the first consumer vehicles could join the Robotaxi fleet in 2Q27. Barclays now reads this as customers using their vehicles as personal Robotaxis, which could drive demand for Tesla vehicles and FSD.

market_movers.rationale: Barclays reiterates Overweight with a $450 target, 18.5% above the $379.74 close on 16-Nov-26. It views Robotaxi inflection as a key catalyst but calls Cybercab capacity expansion a show-me story.

sector_views.rationale: Barclays' industry view for U.S. Autos & Mobility is Neutral.

earnings_insights: At 3Q EPS, Tesla disclosed about 125k annual Cybercab production capacity at Gigafactory Texas. Management said installed capacity was well above that figure and that Cybercab would be built only at the rate the Robotaxi service needs vehicles.

At 3Q EPS, management said the first consumer vehicles could be added to the Robotaxi fleet in 2Q27. Barclays also cited the 3Q release as the last time detailed Robotaxi miles data was provided, through Oct 18.
risk_factors: Barclays lists these downside risks to its TSLA target: reliance on anticipated M&A that has supported the stock, weaker auto demand requiring larger price cuts, slower progress on FSD, Robotaxi and Optimus, and competition from legacy OEM and new-entrant EVs.
Robotaxi operations would need to inflect significantly to justify the Cybercab capacity increase, and EU AV progress appears to trail the US.
Customer-owned Cybercab is restricted to existing Robotaxi geofences and has a $299/month subscription that Musk called too high.
charts_described: Figure 2 plots cumulative Robotaxi miles rising to 3.1 million, with Austin, Dallas/Houston and Orlando/Tampa/Miami shown separately. Data runs through October 18, 2026.
Figure 3 plots weekly Robotaxi miles from 8/10/26 to 10/12/26, rising from 102 thousand to 558 thousand.

Figure 1 lists miles driven as of Oct 18, 2026 and geofence size by city: Austin 2,118,015 miles and 443 sq mi, Dallas 608,130 and 81, Houston 225,964 and 254, Orlando 61,053 and 26, Tampa 53,117 and 24, Miami 46,262 and 59. Fort Worth is 144 sq mi and San Antonio 274 sq mi with no miles listed.

tension_points.bull_case: Higher Cybercab output signals management confidence in Robotaxi scaling. Management said Cybercab is built only at the rate the Robotaxi service needs vehicles, and Barclays sees potential for 300-400k+ per year at Gigafactory Texas.
tension_points.bear_case: The current Robotaxi footprint needs well below the roughly 125k per year capacity, with about 1.3k AVs registered in Texas. Europe has no Robotaxi presence and FSD is not EU-approved, so Barclays suspects early Berlin volumes will be well below 1mn.
tension_points.what_invalidates: US Robotaxi operations would need to inflect significantly to justify the increase in Cybercab production.

theme_stances.key_argument: Robotaxi ODD expansion and 24/7 camera-only operation show continued AV inflection and technical progress.
theme_stances.evidence: We continue to see Robotaxi inflection as a key catalyst for Tesla

theme_stances.key_argument: Cybercab expansion is a show-me story because the current Robotaxi footprint requires well below existing capacity.
